note: Mon 23 Nov 2026 07:03 SGT run, before Asia's open and after Friday's US close. Swept Sunday evening through Monday pre-dawn SGT specifically. Five items below (dated 21-22 Nov) are genuinely new since Sunday's 07:30 SGT brief: China's margin-rule easing and Taiwan's stabilization-fund buying (both policy responses to the AI-rout selloff), Treasury Secretary Bessent's Sunday overtightening warning, the Nvidia SEC-probe story narrowing to Singapore-linked accounting practices, and a fresh Hormuz tanker-military incident. Five items from Friday/Saturday are retained for continuity/relevance (Nvidia's multi-pronged credibility crisis, Fed hike-odds repricing, the gold/silver margin-call debate, Bitcoin's round trip, MP Materials insider buying) and three stale/lower-relevance items (Baltic tanker strike, Russia-Ukraine barrage, US-Venezuela military pact, and a 'nothing found' HK/SG placeholder now superseded by real China/Taiwan news) were dropped this run.

items.headline: Nvidia SEC probe reportedly narrows to accounting/revenue-geography disclosures tied to Singapore entities
items.summary: New reporting (Business Standard, Manila Times, Daily Star, all Nov 22) narrows the previously-known 'SEC probe' to a specific focus: Nvidia's 2025 switch from reporting sales by customer billing address to customer headquarters location, a change that obscured how much revenue flows through Singapore entities, including Megaspeed. Sources say the probe is early-stage and could end without charges.
items.actionable: Adds a Singapore-specific thread (accounting/disclosure practices, not just export-control diversion) to the Megaspeed scandal, raising the chance of follow-on MAS/exchange scrutiny of Singapore-domiciled tech entities -- a reputational tail-risk to watch rather than a direct portfolio holding issue.

items.headline: China eases margin rules, cuts trading fees, floats ChiNext market-maker system to stem $1.7tn tech selloff
items.summary: Shanghai, Shenzhen and Beijing exchanges will cut the minimum margin requirement for buying shares on leverage to 80% from 100%, effective Nov 30, reversing an earlier tightening. Regulators also announced fee cuts and a proposed market-making mechanism for the ChiNext board, framing it as a response to a sharp decline in margin-financing activity after the AI-led global rout wiped out roughly $1.7tn from Chinese tech names.
items.actionable: A modest, targeted liquidity tailwind for HK-listed China tech (Tencent/SMIC/Xiaomi) heading into Monday's open, though it addresses market plumbing, not the underlying AI-capex/Nvidia-scandal overhang that actually drove the selloff.

items.headline: Taiwan widens short-sale ban and deploys NT$500bn stabilization fund after TAIEX's worst weekly drop in 35 years
items.summary: Taiwan's FSC imposed a blanket ban on short sales below the prior day's close and raised short-sale margin requirements to 150% from 130%, after the TAIEX fell 17.5% in a week (worst in 35 years) on AI-trade unwind fears. The NT$500bn (~US$15bn) National Financial Stabilization Fund confirmed it has begun actively buying shares to support the market.
items.actionable: State intervention in the Taiwan tech/semi complex may put a floor under the AI-supply-chain selloff into Monday, a modest sentiment offset for correlated HK/China semis exposure, but the scale of the stabilization effort itself signals how severe the underlying damage is.

items.headline: Treasury Secretary Bessent breaks with hawkish Fed chorus, warns against overtightening
items.summary: On CBS's Face the Nation (Sun Nov 22), Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said 'many people believe' the Fed risks a policy mistake if it overtightens, citing already-substantial tightening in financial conditions and signs of fragility exposed by last week's rout. This is a new, high-profile dovish counter to the recent hawkish Logan/Waller commentary, and traders are reportedly paring back odds of a 50bp December hike in response.
items.actionable: If Bessent's pushback gains traction and trims the odds of a 50bp 'shock' hike at the Dec 8-9 FOMC, it's a tentative positive for the levered silver/miner book, which was hit hardest by hawkish repricing on Friday.

items.headline: Hormuz shipping attacks hit highest level since the conflict began; fresh tanker-military incident Sunday evening
items.summary: UKMTO data shows at least 22 attacks on shipping in/around the Strait of Hormuz in November, the second-highest monthly total since the conflict began, with projectiles striking three tankers Fri/Sat. UKMTO confirmed a fresh 'tanker involved in an incident with military forces' in the Gulf of Oman on Sunday evening, while a separately reported 'Iranian tanker transiting Hormuz' was debunked as a spoofed AIS signal.
items.actionable: A fresh escalation in Hormuz risk going into Monday's Asia open is a tail-risk oil/safe-haven driver that could add support to gold/silver even as it keeps broader risk sentiment fragile -- worth watching given the portfolio's large cash pile and precious-metals tilt.

items.headline: Nvidia's seven-week losing streak (-46%, worst since 2008) now compounds an SEC accounting probe, a California AG subpoena, and a CEO exit -- weekend press digests the pile-up
items.summary: Weekend coverage (24/7 Wall St, Yahoo Finance) framed Nvidia's slide as its longest weekly losing streak since 2008, down 46% over seven weeks and roughly $2.6tn in market value, even as the company's revenue run-rate dwarfs 2008 levels. The pile-up now includes Friday's Reuters-reported SEC accounting probe, a Nov 19 California AG subpoena probing whether ex-CEO Jensen Huang's personal ties to China led to chip/secrets diversion or misleading disclosures, and interim-CEO transition to CFO Colette Kress after Huang's Nov 12 resignation.
items.actionable: No direct holding, but this is now a multi-pronged credibility crisis (SEC + state AG + governance vacuum), not a one-headline shock, which raises the odds of continued AI-capex-narrative contagion into HK tech's own buildout story (0700.HK, 0981.HK) at Monday's Asia open rather than a one-day bounce-back.

items.headline: CME FedWatch odds of a December 25bp hike surge to ~97%, up from 76% a month ago, after Waller floats a 50bp 'shock' move
items.summary: Futures markets now assign roughly 96.9% probability to a quarter-point Fed hike at the Dec 8-9 FOMC (vs 76.3% a month earlier), with hold odds down to about 3% and a 50bp move still a tail outcome; the repricing follows Governor Waller's comments that the Fed may need to shock inflation expectations lower given stubborn ~3% inflation.
items.actionable: A near-certain December hike is now priced, not just debated -- this is the macro backdrop both the owner's SGX bank/REIT exposure (financing costs) and levered silver/miners position (real-rate/dollar channel) must absorb into year-end regardless of how the Nvidia/crypto/oil stories resolve.

items.headline: Gold holds near 14-month low around $3,500-3,538, silver near $41, as weekend commentary splits between 'margin-call capitulation' and 'genuine bear market' reads
items.summary: Spot gold traded around $3,502-3,538/oz over the weekend -- down more than 30% from January's all-time high and its lowest since September 2025 -- while silver held near $41/oz. Kitco's weekend roundup (citing Rich Checkan and others) argued the move is margin-call-driven forced liquidation rather than owners of physical metal exiting, while rising Treasury yields, a firmer dollar, and swelling December-hike bets continue to work against both metals into Monday's Asia open.
items.actionable: Weekend commentary has not resolved the margin-call-vs-bear-market debate that matters most for the owner's leveraged silver/miners book -- gold/silver holding steady rather than extending Friday's rout over the weekend is a mild positive sign for a Monday bounce, but the real-rate/dollar/hike-odds backdrop remains unambiguously hostile.

items.headline: Bitcoin crashes below $57,000 (two-year low $55,130) on a $2.4bn liquidation wave, then rebounds 9% to retake $60,300 as forced selling clears
items.summary: Coinglass data showed $2.4bn in crypto futures liquidated in 24 hours (over $1bn in BTC futures, $545m in ETH futures) as Bitcoin crashed to a two-year low near $55,130 and Ether dropped toward $1,560; Glassnode said the flush cleared a stale cluster of leveraged long bets between $59,000-$62,000 that had built up over months. Bitcoin then rebounded 9% to ~$60,300 by Saturday afternoon as that forced-selling pressure abated, though QCP Capital cautioned a durable recovery needs tech-equity stabilization and returning institutional ETF flows.
items.actionable: Confirms crypto's weekend round trip was leverage-flush-and-release mechanics layered on top of the existing multi-week ETF-outflow/MSCI-removal drain, not a new standalone shock -- the bounce off $55k is a useful reference level, but QCP's conditioning on equity stabilization means Monday's Asia open (and any Nvidia/Broadcom follow-through) is the key swing factor for whether $60k holds.

items.headline: Needham reinstates MP Materials at Buy with a $48/share target as three insiders put $3.6m into shares near the 52-week low
items.summary: Needham resumed coverage of MP Materials with a Buy rating and a $48/share price target, arguing the company is in the early innings of a transformation from miner to vertically integrated rare-earth/magnet supplier, with commercial magnet deliveries to GM expected in Q4 2026 and Apple-linked magnet revenue flagged for H2 2027. Separately, three MP Materials insiders bought a combined $3.6m of stock between Nov 10-17 near the 52-week low, even as the broader rare-earth complex (Critical Metals -8%, USAR -5%) extended its Nov 20 selloff.
items.actionable: Insider buying plus a fresh sell-side reinstatement at a meaningful premium to spot is a genuine fundamental counter-signal for the owner's MP position sitting inside a broader rare-earth group that just got hit by Friday's macro-driven reversal -- worth distinguishing this company-specific bull case from the sector-wide feedstock-delay bear case already flagged on USAR.
